title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page's 'Formulaire de L, Λ'): X is a smooth connected projective variety of dimension n, polarised by ξ_X. L_X is cup product with ξ_X and Λ_X is the corresponding degree −2 operator. Y ⊂ X is a smooth hyperplane section, of dimension n−1, with φ: Y → X the inclusion, restriction φ^* and Gysin map φ_*, so that φ_*φ^* = L_X.

Grothendieck's indexing convention (implicit on both pages). For i ≤ n, P^i(X) is the usual primitive part, Ker Λ = Ker L^{n−i+1} in H^i. For i ≥ n, P^i(X) := Ker(L_X : H^i → H^{i+2}). By hard Lefschetz this equals L^{i−n} P^{2n−i}, the 'top' piece of each Lefschetz string. This gives 2n+1 projectors p_i (0 ≤ i ≤ 2n) with P^n counted once.

The page then does the following.
(1) It records as hypotheses what weak Lefschetz plus hard Lefschetz give:
- φ^*: P^i(X) ≅ P^i(Y) for i ≤ n−2;
- P^{n−1}(X) ↪ P^{n−1}(Y);
- P^i(X) = Ker φ^* for i ≥ n.
It justifies these with the square L_X^{n−i} = φ_* ∘ L_Y^{n−1−i} ∘ φ^*, where φ_* is an isomorphism from H^{2(n−1)−i}(Y) because i ≤ n−2 ⇒ 2(n−1)−i ≥ n. It also uses the triangle L_X = φ_*φ^*, with φ_*: H^j(Y) ≅ H^{j+2}(X) for j ≥ n.
(2) It writes the decompositions
- H^*(X) = ⊕_{i+j≤n} L^j P^i(X) = ⊕_{i+j≤n−1} L^j P^i(X) ⊕ ⊕_{j≥n} P^j(X);
- H^*(Y) = ⊕_{i+j≤n−1} L_Y^j P^i(Y).
The pieces with i+j = n are exactly the renamed P^{n+j}(X).
(3) Corollary: φ^* maps the bigraded summand ⊕_{i+j≤n−1} L_X^j P^i(X) bihomogeneously into H^*(Y). It is an isomorphism on every component except L^0 P^{n−1}(X) → P^{n−1}(Y), where it is only injective.
(4) Corollary: Ker φ^* = Ker L_X = ⊕_{j≥n} P^j(X). The cokernel is concentrated in degree n−1: E^{n−1} = H^{n−1}(Y)/Im H^{n−1}(X) = P^{n−1}(Y)/Im P^{n−1}(X), which is ≅ Ker(φ_*: H^{n−1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X)), i.e. the vanishing cohomology.

Purpose: this is bookkeeping for the induction 'A(X×X) and C(Y) ⇒ C(X)' stated on the previous page. It shows how φ^*, φ_*, L, Λ and the projectors p_i relate when one passes from a hyperplane section to the ambient variety. This is the mechanism behind the inductive arguments for the Lefschetz-type standard conjecture in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1968/69) and Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968).
errors: In the commutative square, the transcription's exponents and degrees do not match the stated implication i ≤ n−2 ⇒ 2(n−1)−i ≥ n. The consistent version is L_X^{n−i}: H^i(X) → H^{2n−i}(X), L_Y^{n−1−i}: H^i(Y) → H^{2(n−1)−i}(Y), and Gysin φ_{2(n−1)−i}: H^{2(n−1)−i}(Y) → H^{2n−i}(X). The '+i' in H^{2(n-1)+i}(Y) and the '+1, +2' in L_X^{n-i+1}, H^{2n-i+2} are either misreadings or slips; the sign must be −i.

The first Corollary as literally written claims an isomorphism of bigraded objects onto H^*(Y). This fails in bidegree (n−1, 0), where P^{n−1}(X) → P^{n−1}(Y) is only a monomorphism. Grothendieck corrects this himself in the following line ('induit un mono ... L^0 P^{n−1}(X) → P^{n−1}(Y)'). The cokernel E^{n−1} computed at the bottom confirms the correction.

The identification coker ≅ Ker(Gysin) in degree n−1 needs H^{n−1}(Y) = Im φ^* ⊕ Ker φ_*. This holds without positivity: φ_*φ^* = L_X is injective on H^{n−1}(X), and dimensions add up because Gysin H^{n−1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X) is surjective. It is not stated explicitly, but it is correct.

ideas.what: Uniform indexing P^i(X), 0 ≤ i ≤ 2n: primitive (Ker Λ) for i ≤ n, Ker L for i ≥ n. This gives projectors p_i and a decomposition H^* = ⊕_{i+j≤n−1} L^j P^i ⊕ ⊕_{j≥n} P^j.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz decomposition / sl_2 (Lefschetz) module structure, primitive and 'coprimitive' parts
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; Hodge; sl_2 formalism by Chern, Weil, Serre (1950s)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) uses primitive decomposition and Λ, but this specific 0..2n indexing convention is unsure

ideas.what: Restriction to a smooth hyperplane section is an isomorphism on primitive parts below the middle, injective at n−1, with kernel Ker L_X. Proved via the factorisation L_X^{n−i} = φ_* L_Y^{n−1−i} φ^*.
ideas.modern_name: Weak (Lefschetz hyperplane) theorem combined with hard Lefschetz
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lefschetz; Andreotti–Frankel, Bott; SGA 4 / Deligne (Weil II) in the ℓ-adic setting
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures paper (1968/69); Kleiman, Dix exposés (1968), §1–2

ideas.what: Cokernel of restriction in degree n−1 = vanishing cohomology = Ker of Gysin H^{n−1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X).
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 (exposés of Deligne, Katz); also used in Weil I

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping combining weak and hard Lefschetz for a hyperplane section, in support of the known induction 'C(Y) + A(X×X) ⇒ C(X)'. That induction is in substance in Grothendieck's 1968 standard conjectures paper and in Kleiman's exposition. The only slightly idiosyncratic feature is the symmetric 0..2n indexing of 'primitive' pieces, which is a notational convenience rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Top square: should read H^i(X) --L_X^{n−i}--> H^{2n−i}(X), φ^*: H^i(X) → H^i(Y), H^i(Y) --L_Y^{n−1−i}--> H^{2(n−1)−i}(Y), φ_{2(n−1)−i} back up. The '2' marks on the vertical arrows are probably '≀' (isomorphism) signs, and the side condition is i ≤ n−2.
'c'est l'idéal de L_X' is more plausibly 'c'est le noyau de L_X, i.e.' (Ker φ^* = Ker L_X = ⊕_{j≥n} P^j(X)).
'Ex. Non—' is likely a heading such as 'Ex.' or 'Exemple' followed by 'Notons' / 'On a'.
In the Corollary's cokernel line, 'Im H^{n−1}(X)' and 'Im P^{n−1}(X)' are images under φ^*. The last line reads Ker(φ_Gys : H^{n−1}(Y) → H^{n+1}(X)).
